The Tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index fell 1.5% on Tuesday, with NVDA and SPCX down 6%, and ANT slipping 7%.

El-Erian pointed investors to a post from Yorkville analyst Dan Ives from last week in which the analyst noted that the selloff in the market is caused by not one but a "perfect storm" of factors.

Ross Gerber of Gerber Kawasaki pointed to both SpaceX and Anthropic trading below their offering prices as evidence that markets, rather than underwriters, ultimately set valuations.

The Tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index fell 1.5% on Tuesday, paring back some of the 7% gains on Monday, in a move economist Mohamed El-Erian termed a sign that warning signals in the market extend well beyond chipmaker Nvidia.

In a post on X, the Wharton school professor noted that the key question is whether those deteriorating technical conditions now risk feeding into weaker fundamentals.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Source: Mohamed El-Erian/ X

El-Erian also highlighted that Anthropic shares had fallen below its IPO price of $83 on Tuesday, continuing a rapid descent after the stock opened above $110 in its mid-November debut. The AI company, which raised one of the largest offerings on record, has now given back a substantial portion of its early gains, trading as low as the mid-$75s during the session. El-Erian had previously noted that Anthropic's post-IPO path appeared to be tracking SpaceX's trajectory after its IPO, but at a faster pace.

The Nasdaq Composite had risen 7% on Monday, after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang in less than two weeks of his exit following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia itself rose over 31% on Monday, and caused a larger rally in AI and tech stocks. The rally faded on Tuesday, and Nvidia shares slipped 6%.

El-Erian pointed investors to a post from Yorkville analyst Dan Ives from last week in which the analyst noted that the selloff in the market is caused by not one but a "perfect storm" of factors — including post-midterm election policy concerns, China-related regulatory worries in semiconductors, fund performance pain, and sticky inflation.

Markets Set Valuations, Says Gerber

Anthropic is not alone in trading below its IPO price. SpaceX shares closed 6% lower on Tuesday at $125.81, below its June IPO price of $135.

Ross Gerber of Gerber Kawasaki pointed to both SpaceX and Anthropic trading below their offering prices as evidence that markets, rather than underwriters, ultimately set valuations.

title: How Much Is Nvidia Stock Worth Now That Jensen Huang Is Back?
detail:
How Much Is Nvidia Stock Worth Now That Jensen Huang Is Back?
Adria Cimino, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 6:30 PM EST 5 min read
NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When most investors think of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), they think of Jensen Huang. That's why, when the famous chief executive officer stepped down and then came back to his post 11 days later, the stock reacted. Huang's departure resulted in declines, and his return resulted in significant gains -- the stock soared more than 30% in one trading session.

We all know that CEOs are important, but Huang's visionary role at Nvidia, as well as his prominence in the artificial intelligence (AI) space worldwide, make him a key player in this high-growth field. Without his leadership, Nvidia shareholders worried that the company might not continue to expand at the same pace and in the same direction.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, clearly, investors celebrated Huang's return. Now let's consider how much Nvidia stock is worth with Huang back at the helm.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

Jensen Huang leads Nvidia's success story

First, though, let's take a look at the Nvidia story so far, including the recent turmoil. Nvidia has trailblazed in AI, with its early entry into the AI chip market and innovations that have kept it ahead of rivals. This has resulted in jaw-dropping earnings growth, and this deep involvement in AI has transformed Jensen Huang into an expert in the field. His knowledge and visibility about what's ahead have made him a valuable asset -- and one that investors weren't eager to replace.

That's why when he resigned following allegations of two affairs, the stock slid, and investors questioned the ability of the company to continue with the same momentum. Huang's reinstatement reassured investors, as we can see through the stock's performance. It's important to keep in mind, however, that Nvidia isn't out of the woods yet. The company is investigating Huang's relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence says is a spy for China. And lawmakers have called for Huang to testify on the matter -- that should unfold early next month. Meanwhile, press reports say that regulators have opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices.

All of this, as well as investors' growing caution regarding AI, may periodically weigh on the stock price. Tech giants aim to spend more than $700 billion on the infrastructure build-out this year, and investors worry that the revenue opportunity may fall short. This concern has represented a headwind for AI stocks in general since the start of this year.

Chip stocks' Nvidia-fueled rally reversed on Tuesday

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA)'s decision to bring back CEO Jensen Huang set off a huge rally across chip stocks on Monday as investors reacted to the stunning reversal just a week after the board told investors it wasn't an option. The Nasdaq had its best day since April of 2025.

But that rally reversed sharply today as investors digested what his return will mean in the long term and how it will affect chip rivals -- like Intel.

Intel's new foundry customer has an unclear payoff

Just last week, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company had landed its first outside customer for 18A-P, an advanced manufacturing process important to the company's turnaround efforts. It's a positive step, but details were light, so it's unclear how much financial impact it will actually have.

Intel's foundry business posted a $1.85 billion operating loss last quarter, with the company's finance chief indicating the company probably won't generate positive free cash flow -- the cash left over after paying for investments like new factories -- next year as it keeps investing in manufacturing.

title: A scandal like the one haunting Nvidia just reached AMD, its biggest rival
detail:
A scandal like the one haunting Nvidia just reached AMD, its biggest rival
Peace Longe, Celine Provini
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 6:17 PM EST 4 min read
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped as much as 11% on Nov. 19, 2026. They dropped after a short-selling firm claimed that the chipmaker might have deeper ties to China than it has disclosed to investors.

After the report, CNBC confirmed that AMD closed at $489.19 that day, after dropping about 7.7%. That one afternoon wiped out close to $70 billion of the company's market value, which was above $800 billion before the trading day opened. 

Also read: CoreWeave stuns Wall Street as Nvidia scandal deepens

The short seller claims that sent AMD stock tumbling

Hunterbrook Media published the report on Nov. 19. In it, the short seller claimed that AMD is exposed to Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, a company the U.S. Commerce Department added to its Entity List in March 2025.

And American firms are restricted from selling technology to the names on that list without special approval.

Now Hunterbrook is saying IEIT posted at least six server updates that contain AMD's newer "TurinPI" firmware. AMD first released that specific firmware in July 2026, Wccftech reported.

The report flags AMD's 2025 revenue from China and Hong Kong, which reached $7.75 billion, or 22.4% of total sales. It also highlighted its 2025 Singapore revenue, which came in at 12.4% of the company's fiscal 2025 revenue, according to AMD's 10-K filing with the SEC.

AMD CEO Lisa Su has led the chipmaker's growth into the artificial intelligence market.Austin American-Statesman/Hearst Newspapers / Getty Images
Why this reaches past Wall Street and into regular wallets

AMD designs the chips inside many of our everyday devices, including personal computers, Sony's PlayStation, Microsoft's Xbox, and large facilities like data center servers. The stock also ranks among the largest companies on the Nasdaq 100. 

The Nasdaq 100 shows up inside almost every major retirement fund in the country. So when AMD drops nearly 8% in one session, it reduces — albeit not significantly — the savings of people who might not even pay attention to the market. 

AMD's response and where Lisa Su stands

AMD responded to the report, saying, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," CNBC reported. The company added that it "complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations" and has "rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

Hunterbrook itself admitted that its findings do not prove AMD broke any rules, only that the software link deserves a closer look, Yahoo Finance reported.
